entries.appliesTo: operators of public-facing conversational AI services

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 48-2103(1) — 'an operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose that the conversational AI service is artificial intelligence'
dutySources.crisis-protocol: § 48-2103(2) — 'An operator shall adopt a protocol for the conversational AI service to respond to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation that includes but is not limited to making reasonable efforts to provide a response to users that refers them to crisis service providers'
dutySources.content-safeguards: § 48-2104(3) — 'an operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent the conversational AI service from: (a) Producing visual material of sexually explicit conduct'

sources.scope: § 48-2102(2)(a) — 'accessible to the general public and that primarily simulates human conversation and interaction through textual, visual, or aural communications'
sources.ageFocus: § 48-2103 — 'OPERATOR REQUIREMENTS' (duties bind as to all users); § 48-2104 — 'OPERATOR REQUIREMENTS -- MINORS' adds minor-specific duties
sources.crisisProtocol: § 48-2103(2) — 'shall adopt a protocol for the conversational AI service to respond to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation'
sources.parentalTools: § 48-2104(5) — 'An operator shall also offer related tools to the parents or guardians of minor account holders thirteen (13) years of age and older, as appropriate based on relevant risks.'
sources.engagementLimits: § 48-2104(2) — 'the operator shall not provide the user with points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals with the intent to encourage increased engagement with the conversational AI service'
sources.contentSafeguards: § 48-2104(4) — 'shall institute reasonable measures to prevent a conversational AI service from generating statements that would lead reasonable persons to believe that they are interacting with a human'
sources.ageThreshold: § 48-2102(4) — 'actual knowledge or reasonable certainty that the individual is under eighteen (18) years of age'
sources.penaltyMax: § 48-2105(1) — 'civil penalties of one thousand dollars ($1,000) per violation, not to exceed five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000) per operator, or actual damages, whichever is greater'
sources.enforcer: § 48-2105(2) — 'Civil penalties for violations of the provisions of this chapter are to be sought by the attorney general.'

flags: penalty structure: $1,000 per violation capped at $500,000 per operator, 'or actual damages, whichever is greater' (§ 48-2105(1)); penaltyMax codes the aggregate cap (highest stated fine); injunction also available

aiDisclosure lossy: § 48-2104(1) lets the operator choose 'a persistent visible disclaimer' OR both session-start and a repeat 'at least every three (3) hours in a continuous conversational AI service interaction'; coded session-start as the closest single enum

general-audience AI disclosure (§ 48-2103(1)) is conditional — required only 'If reasonable persons would be misled to believe that they are interacting with a human'; no aiDisclosure enum captures this trigger

ageFocus lossy: baseline duties (§ 48-2103) bind operators as to all users, while § 48-2104 layers minor-specific duties (disclosure cadence, engagement rewards, content safeguards, parental tools); coded all-users

§ 48-2103(3) prohibits knowingly programming the service to make any representation 'that explicitly indicates that the conversational AI service is designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care' — a conduct prohibition fitting no listed duty key
no private right of action: 'Nothing in this chapter shall be construed as creating a private right of action' (§ 48-2105(2))

developer safe harbor: 'This chapter shall not create liability for the developer of an AI model for any violation of this chapter by a conversational AI system that is made available to the public by a third-party operator' (§ 48-2105(3))

parental tools tiered at age 13 (§ 48-2104(5)): under-13 account holders' parents/guardians get privacy and account-settings tools; parents of minors 13 and older get tools 'as appropriate based on relevant risks'

broad exclusions from 'conversational AI service' (§ 48-2102(2)(b)): developer/researcher tools, embedded features, game-limited chatbots, narrow-topic bots, business/enterprise deployments, voice assistants, internal-use and customer-service bots
